content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Corpus Christi

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: Verify you meet PMI's education and project-management experience requirements for the PMP credential. Review the specific thresholds based on your degree level, then document your qualifying work hours. PMI sets these standards; Granite PM Academy's advisors can help you assess your profile before enrollment.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Boot Camp. Attend all sessions synchronously with experienced instructors who guide you through the PMBOK Guide framework, exam domains, and real-world application. You'll earn the formal education hours PMI requires to sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: File your PMP application directly with PMI, confirming your eligibility and project experience. Pay the associated exam fee through PMI's portal. Granite PM Academy staff can answer procedural questions, though you manage the submission and payment independently with the Project Management Institute.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for Your Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor support—to solidify your readiness. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. On exam day, demonstrate your mastery of project-management principles across all five process groups and ten knowledge areas.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) throughout the standard three-year renewal cycle. Pursue continuing education, conference attendance, or volunteer project-leadership roles to stay current in the profession. Renew your credential with PMI before expiration to keep the PMP active on your resume.
